headline: Source: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin stretches list of trade options to 10 teams
take:
Dylan Larkin has told the Red Wings he would accept a trade to at least seven more teams, bringing his list of options to 10, per ESPN. The Athletic reports the expanded list includes 10 U.S. teams, and notes he has scored 30-plus goals in five straight seasons with Detroit.

The numbers here suggest a player whose results are lagging his play. Larkin has one goal and five points in seven games so far this season, but his own expected goals (a measure of the quality of the chances he gets) are 1.79, so he is 0.79 goals below what those chances should have produced. Last season he scored 34 goals in 74 games, and his shot quality gives no sign of a decline. Detroit controls 51% of the quality chances with him on the ice at five-on-five, a slightly better than even split. For fantasy owners, the slow start looks more like bad luck than a drop in his level, and a trade would not change that. For the Red Wings, DET sits at 3-3-3 with 49.7% of the expected goals overall, and they are 7.1 goals below expectation, so they are underperforming too. Moving their top forward would leave them thin.
